prerequisites: Basic notions of logic and mathematics are recommended.

learning_outcomes.text: Students will have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is usually at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects that imply knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

Students will know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competences that are usually demonstrated through the elaboration and defense of arguments and the resolution of problems within their area of study.
Students will have developed those learning skills necessary to undertake further studies with a high degree of autonomy.

Choose and apply the most appropriate methods and techniques to analyze and solve problems defined by data that represent a challenge due to their volume, velocity, variety, or heterogeneity, including computational, mathematical, statistical, and signal processing methods.

Possess the experimental and analytical skills to work autonomously, being able to plan experiments and describe, analyze, evaluate, and interpret the resulting information to propose alternative and novel solutions to known and/or emerging problems.
Create models and make decisions based on available data, combining acquired knowledge and being able to apply new knowledge to solve problems.
Ability to integrate into a multidisciplinary team within the framework of a data science project.
Ability to express the results of data processing clearly and convincingly, both in writing and orally.
Know the fundamentals of programming and basic algorithmic techniques and apply them using the most relevant programming languages in the field of data science and engineering.
Understand the concept of an algorithm and the process of abstraction of a problem in programming.
Identify the software development process and its location within the general Software Engineering process.
Know the elementary data structures provided by a structured programming language.
Manage the elementary control structures of a structured programming language.
Abstract an operation. Design functions, including simple recursive functions.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to programming: basic concepts and languages.
Elementary data structures: lists, tuples, dictionaries.
Introduction to OOP: classes, objects, methods.

assessment_methods.method: Participation in forums/online activities (e.g., quizzes, test exams)
Continuous assessment (resolution of programming exercises in laboratory)

assessment_rules: For ordinary assessment, the final grade is calculated as (0.05 x A) + (0.10 x B) + (0.40 x C) + (0.45 x D), where A is attendance, B is online participation, C is continuous assessment, and D is the final exam. A minimum of 4 out of 10 points is required on the final exam (D) to pass. For differentiated assessment, the final grade is (0.50 x ET) + (0.50 x EP), with a minimum of 4 out of 10 required on the theoretical final exam (ET). In extraordinary calls, if continuous assessment (A+B+C) is passed with 5 or more, the final grade is (Continuous Assessment + Theoretical Exam) / 2, with a minimum of 4 on the theoretical exam. Otherwise, for other students (including differentiated assessment), the final grade is (0.50 x Theoretical Exam) + (0.50 x Practical Exam), requiring a minimum of 4 out of 10 on both the theoretical (ET) and practical (EP) exams.
